answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable bond before it may submit work, then slash that bond when independently sampled audits show fabricated results or coordinated duplicate claims. The audit links claims to outputs, not just profile names, so a sparrow account cannot evade scrutiny by copying a mirror identity or using a forge. Creating many Sybils therefore means locking up more capital, while detected fraud destroys the attacker’s stake and makes repetition costly.
